summary.name: How Embracing Continuous Release Reduced Change Complexity
summary.one_liner: A 2014 USENIX talk by Google SRE Caskey Dickson describing an experience report on automating continuous release engineering for an in-house deployment to a fleet of under 1,000 nodes.
use_cases: Understanding how automated continuous release replaced quarterly manual releases
Learning about promoting CI green builds through test, staging and production
Reviewing benefits and failure modes of automated release pipelines
Planning release automation for a moderate sized server fleet
summary.what_it_does: The talk is an experience report on using continuous release engineering to automate administration of an in-house software deployment to a fleet of fewer than 1,000 nodes at Google. An automatic process takes green builds from the continuous integration system and promotes them to test, staging and production. Unless automated checks detect an error, committed code reaches production about 14 days later. The talk contrasts this with the earlier manual periodic releases, which occurred roughly quarterly. It also covers unanticipated benefits and new failure modes the automation introduced.
notable: Describes Google's automatic promotion of green CI builds to test, staging and production
Committed code reaches production in about 14 days unless automated checks catch an error
Compares automated continuous release with earlier roughly quarterly manual releases
Presented at USENIX in Seattle, November 2014
caveats: This is a conference talk summary, not a software tool; no downloadable product is described
Scope is a fleet of less than 1,000 nodes, per the abstract
